content:
Hi all.

I ran a mechanical sweep for theorems whose setting is stronger than their proof needs (weaken the hypothesis, re-run the proof, keep it if it compiles).

None of the findings is new mathematics (they are internal lemmas) and this question isn't new [1].

Sample: 29,261 theorems across 18 subject areas. 431 survive weakening. The sample is what the search could reach.

In 87.5% of the rows, the weakened version has the same proof term, so the assumption was genuinely unused.

I ran the same thing over Tau Ceti [2]: 0.45% of attempts versus 0.40% here, intervals [0.36, 0.57] and [0.36, 0.44], p = 0.35. No measurable difference. Whatever this is, it isn't a habit of one library's authors.

I could send 33 single-line PRs but of course I don't dump on reviewers without a word. They were found at v4.33.1. I re-checked them against master (633b366493, v4.34.0-rc2): 33 of the original 36 still apply and the whole file builds. Of the 3 that did not survive, one is #_42214 (someone removed the same unused section variable and went further).

The repo with all the things is https://github.com/carlok/unused-assumptions

While there was AI usage in the project, I wrote this post by hand per the guidelines.

Thank you for your work.

[1] Answered analytically for Mathlib in 2021. The brute-force version was run on a different library in 2013 and judged too slow for Mathlib. I spent many CPU days but with a single PC.

[2] As you know, their proof is AI generated and that is the interesting comparison.

Hey, could you show an example, in the form of a github diff? (fork mathlib, make the changes on a branch, link to the compare page for your branch)

How does this compare to previous efforts to automatically generalize typeclass assumptions?
Ooh it's pretty cool that everything in file#Topology/EMetricSpace/Pi could just take [EDist α] instead of [TopologicalSpace α] [WeakPseudoEMetricSpace α]

Hi and thanks. I created the diff and that spotted a correction [1].
It is here

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/compare/master...carlok:mathlib4:weaken-unused-typeclass-assumptions

About your second question: the prior art is at https://github.com/carlok/unused-assumptions#prior-art

[1] 3 patches turn out to be alternatives on the same variable line

Cool! I think that most of these would be great to have.
(btw AFAIK CompleteSemilatticeSup is frowned upon)

To clarify, this is a sample of a small part of Mathlib right? I expect that there are lots of such possible generalizations in the rest of Mathlib

Thanks for CompleteSemilatticeSup
I'm making a PR taking it into account.
The project worked on nearly all files, a sixth of theorems, and the limit is the substitution table.
Yes, there are interesting things to do described in the repo and its LaTeX file.
See:
https://github.com/carlok/unused-assumptions/tree/main/paper
I also have a "dual" repo named
https://github.com/carlok/unstated-conclusions
which contributed two measurements to this paper.
I will not be online in the upcoming hours.

I agree some of these look useful, although some are not helpful, eg changing AddCommGroup + Module to AddCommMonoid + Module. I think this has been discussed somewhere on zulip, but if not @Eric Wieser gave a good explanation today.
I'd welcome a PR doing the changes for Mathlib/Order/Antichain.lean, Mathlib/Data/Finset/Pairwise.lean and Mathlib/Order/Monotone/Extension.lean (picked by scrolling through and looking at ones I'm confident are improvements). But be careful to adjust the surrounding sections appropriately, especially looking at their names to ensure the file's structure remains sensible

Moderation note: your initial message #mathlib4 > unused hypotheses: 431 in a 29k sample, and 33 one-line PRs @ 💬 shows strong signs of being partially AI-written. Please note that using AI to write comments here (be it fully, partially or for editing) is against the rules on this site. Use your own words instead.
Next time, I'll have to delete your messages and suspend your account.

Thank you @Bhavik Mehta
I created this https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/43660
I hope it is close enough to your suggestions
